source.title: Large Language Models Encode Semantics and Alignment in Linearly Separable Representations
source.authors: Baturay Saglam; Paul Kassianik; Blaine Nelson; Sajana Weerawardhena; Yaron Singer; Amin Karbasi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether harmful intent is recoverable from hidden representations and relates that signal to refusal behavior, using a trained MLP probe and refusal evaluations rather than the original difference-in-means direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper does not find, ablate, or add a single refusal direction, nor test weight-edit removal or jailbreak suppression of that direction. Its relevant evidence is the hidden-state harmfulness classifier and the reported contrast between recognized harmful intent and the base model's compliance with harmful injections. Other geometry and guardrail results are not evidence for the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. only in related work. It never builds, ablates, adds or edits a refusal direction. Its safety evidence is a supervised nonlinear MLP guardrail on Llama 3.1-8B final-layer states, trained on WildJailbreak labels, plus base-model refusal rates shown only in a figure. A label-trained probe recovering harm information is the study's own detection method, not a measure of the model's harm judgment set against a measured refusal representation. So it does not test V5 or any other version; the related finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that semantic domains, CoT instructions and safety-related prompt types form linearly separable clusters in hidden states across 11 models, sharpening in deeper layers. They also conclude that a 13.9M-parameter MLP guardrail on final-layer Llama 3.1-8B states raises refusal of harmful prompts and injections beyond Llama Guard 3, cutting harmful responses over 2×, at some cost of conservatism on benign injections. They make no claim about a single refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a trained nonlinear MLP on final-layer hidden states to classify prompt intent and narrative, then evaluates a guardrail; it does not construct or intervene on a difference-in-means refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported guardrail has a trade-off on adversarial prompts: it is more conservative toward benign injections. Safety-representation and guardrail experiments are limited to WildJailbreak and the instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B.

fits_no_version.finding: A supervised MLP on Llama 3.1-8B Instruct final-layer hidden states recovers harmful intent of WildJailbreak prompts, including harmful injections (1805/2000 correctly classified). Yet the base model often complies with such injections (Figure 5, values not stated).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-intent information remains decodable from pre-generation hidden states of jailbreak prompts that the aligned model nonetheless complies with.

record.problems: Safety-representation and guardrail evidence uses one model and depends on WildJailbreak, as the paper notes. Refusal-rate values are shown in Figure 5 but are not stated numerically in the text. The probe is trained on hidden states and does not isolate a causal refusal mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted. The paper's semantic-domain separability, chain-of-thought steering, and guardrail results that do not directly address the tested harmfulness/refusal distinction were not entered as claim rows.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction, ablation, addition or capability check. The only steering is a CoT centroid vector, unrelated to refusal.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing a refusal direction, nor of training against ablation.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction refusal structure.
No measured refusal representation set against the model's own harm representation. There is no causal or per-item dissociation, only a label-trained probe.
No transfer across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct.

record.verdict_notes: Re-gated from tests/T2 to cites_only/T6. The reader's V5 labels rested on the study's own detector metrics and a figure-only refusal rate, with no refusal representation measured. The intro's 96.7% accuracy figure is inconsistent with the 94.06% in Section 7.1 and Table 5. The ethics section mentions unreported harmful-to-benign steering that produced gibberish; it has no data and is not a row.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction is measured or causally ablated/added; preservation of general capability under such an intervention is not tested.
No weight edit or abliteration is tested.
The paper does not test whether attacks suppress a refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The paper describes safety-prompt clusters but does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or dominant direction plus additional directions.

The study does not directly compare a model's endogenous harmfulness judgment with a separately measured refusal-decision representation or establish a causal decomposition; it tests harmful-intent classification from hidden states and reports base-model compliance with harmful injections.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
The study does not compare refusal training procedures or training stages to test whether they determine the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning-model refusal-direction test is conducted.

rows.subject: instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: A 6-layer MLP classifies final-layer hidden states into direct/injection narrative and benign/harmful intent classes.

conditions.value: four: direct benign, direct harmful, benign injections, harmful injections

rows.measure: Four-class classification accuracy and macro F1
rows.note: The authors also report that the probe classifies harmfulness regardless of adversarial framing; the classifier is trained on hidden states, not a refusal direction.
rows.check: This is the study's own guardrail performance (94.06% accuracy, macro F1 0.8767), not a measure of a refusal direction or a harm-vs-refusal separation. The intro reports 96.7% overall accuracy, which conflicts with Section 7.1 and Table 5 (3960/4210 = 94.06%).

rows.subject: instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: The four-class MLP's benign-versus-harmful intent distinction is evaluated on final-layer hidden states.

conditions.value: benign versus harmful intent, across narrative framing

rows.measure: ROC-AUC and macro F1 for benign-versus-harmful distinction
rows.note: The paper interprets this as evidence that harmfulness is clearly encoded in the latent representations regardless of adversarial framing.
rows.check: Method-performance metric (ROC-AUC 0.9813, macro F1 0.9384) of a supervised nonlinear probe trained on external harm labels. It shows harm information is decodable, not that the model's own harm judgment is encoded apart from its refusal decision.

rows.subject: instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: The four-class MLP classifies benign-injection prompts from final-layer hidden states.
rows.note: The study reports weaker classification for benign injections than for the direct classes; this qualifies how consistently the probe distinguishes intent in this prompt condition.
rows.check: Per-class guardrail metric (benign injections P 0.49, R 0.74, F1 0.59). This is the method's weakness, not a qualification of any claim version. It should not carry a V5 limits_scope label.

rows.subject: instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: The base model's responses to harmful injections are classified as refusals or non-refusals.
rows.value: The paper states that models tend to generate compliant responses to harmful injections; refusal-rate values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper presents this alongside the finding that the hidden-state guardrail can recognize adversarial harmful intent even when the base model complies; the figure does not provide textual numeric values.
rows.check: Base-model refusal rate on harmful injections is figure-only with no stated number. The paper gives no per-prompt joint of probe-detected harm and model compliance, so it cannot show dissociation between harm encoding and refusal.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Harmful-injection prompts for the instruct-finetuned Llama 3.1-8B
reader_labels.reason: The hidden-state probe classifies harmful intent with high reported performance (r1, r2), while the paper reports that the base model can comply with harmful injections (r4), indicating that an intent signal can be present without refusal.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The probe's benign-injection class has lower reported performance than the overall and binary intent metrics (r3), so the signal is not equally clear across all prompt types.
